input.text: Prepare a 5-minute talk for engineers on how skillpp works inside, from docs/architecture.md. Start with an outline of at most 6 slides for me to approve.

steps.reply:
Draft outline. 6 slides max, ~50s each.

**Slide 1 — What skillpp does**
Turn Claude Code sessions into reusable skills. Capture → judge → segment → match → ledger → draft.

**Slide 2 — The pipeline**
ASCII diagram from architecture.md. Hooks (UserPromptSubmit/PostToolUse) → session JSON → detached `fold-session` → ledger → `draft` agent → `drafts/<id>/SKILL.md`.

**Slide 3 — Why nothing model-calls in a hook**
Hooks never raise, exit 0. Judge/embeddings/naming all in detached fold worker. Sessions without verdict are **held**, banked next `SessionStart`. No guessing.

**Slide 4 — Module map**
Tour of the boxes: `capture`, `boundary`, `segment`, `matching`, `ledger`, `local`, `sanitize`, `cli/web`. One-line each. Show one rule = one place (`is_read_only`, `DESTRUCTIVE`, `judge_gap`).

**Slide 5 — Rules code keeps**
Hook never raises. Nothing without `--apply`. Nothing self-installs. Scrub before disk. Hold rather than guess. Precision > recall on merge.

**Slide 6 — Measuring a change**
Unit suite = stubbed, fast, correctness only. Real quality = `score.py`, `recurrence.py`, `judge_replay.py`, `merge_ladder.py` on fixtures + Ollama. One change, compare `expected.json`, log in `benchmarks.md`.

Approve or edit which slide?

**Slide 4 — Design invariants** *(new, replaces module map)*
- Hook never raises.
- Nothing without `--apply` (dry-run default).
- Nothing self-installs; promotion stays user's call.
- Scrub before disk (`sanitize.scrub`).
- Hold rather than guess (guessed boundaries scored worse than none).
- Precision > recall on merge (dup visible, wrong merge silent).

**Slide 5 — One place for each rule**
Single-answer principle: `segment.is_read_only`, `signals.DESTRUCTIVE`, `boundary.judge_gap`, `install.installed_events`, `capture.fold_session`. Reuse, don't rewrite.

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor

prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

BLANK = prs.slide_layouts[6]

TITLE_COLOR = RGBColor(0x1F, 0x2A, 0x44)
BODY_COLOR = RGBColor(0x30, 0x30, 0x30)
ACCENT = RGBColor(0x2E, 0x7D, 0x6B)


def add_title(slide, text):
    box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.6), Inches(0.35), Inches(12.1), Inches(0.9))
    tf = box.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    r = p.add_run()
    r.text = text
    r.font.size = Pt(36)
    r.font.bold = True
    r.font.color.rgb = TITLE_COLOR


def add_subtitle(slide, text):
    box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.6), Inches(1.25), Inches(12.1), Inches(0.5))
    tf = box.text_frame
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    r = p.add_run()
    r.text = text
    r.font.size = Pt(18)
    r.font.italic = True
    r.font.color.rgb = ACCENT


def add_bullets(slide, bullets, top=Inches(1.9), left=Inches(0.7), width=Inches(12.0), height=Inches(5.2), size=20):
    box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = box.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, item in enumerate(bullets):
        p = tf.paragraphs[0] if i == 0 else tf.add_paragraph()
        p.space_after = Pt(8)
        if isinstance(item, tuple):
            head, rest = item
            r1 = p.add_run()
            r1.text = f"• {head}"
            r1.font.size = Pt(size)
            r1.font.bold = True
            r1.font.color.rgb = TITLE_COLOR
            r2 = p.add_run()
            r2.text = f" — {rest}"
            r2.font.size = Pt(size)
            r2.font.color.rgb = BODY_COLOR
        else:
            r = p.add_run()
            r.text = f"• {item}"
            r.font.size = Pt(size)
            r.font.color.rgb = BODY_COLOR
